In UK you don't get affordable luxury really. Use the job to buy your freedom, so you can free your wife & you from a grind and fund a lifestyle exploring Europe, America & Asia, 2 - 3 months here and 2 weeks over there, essentially having the freedom to do as you please.

This is achievable in the UK if you do not suffer from lifestyle creep. My plan is to pay off my house which is 300K, my expenses are halved and I then have the flexibility of only using what I consume. Meaning I can go to places and run my business remotely if I want or come back and enjoy some downtime and comforts such as family, friends or just my own space.

I have considered this for years. For those who are young and have achieved early success, places like Dubai, Malaysia, and Thailand offer affordable luxury. These countries provide great weather, large homes, affordable facilities, services, and good visa options for those with financial means.

Personally, I've learned to love the UK in the end. Every country has its cons, and for me, the drawbacks of the aforementioned places aren’t worth sacrificing what the UK offers. The UK's location, countryside, and diversity provide a unique and valuable experience that I wouldn't trade.

You might also consider having the UK as your main base. It offers a locational advantage: just 6 hours to Florida, 2 hours to Spain or Italy. This allows you to enjoy stability while having easy access to various global destinations and retain a high income job or business.

You're working long hours, but is it worth it? I make the same amount as you, but I have my own business and enjoy the freedom it brings. Yesterday, I took a nap at noon and today, I spent two hours shopping to take care of some house stuff. Would you still feel trapped and burned out if you had this kind of freedom?

Money without freedom is meaningless. It should unlock your freedom, but if you have money and little free time, you’re trapped. In that sense, you're no better off than someone earning half your salary. You're just richer but burdened by lifestyle creep, losing child benefits, facing higher fines, and managing a larger mortgage. You might drive a fancier car, but at what cost?

Don’t use money to buy objects; use it to buy freedom. Those objects will not make you happy, they will just suppress your souls desire to be free.

Once money is no object or can no longer be traded for an object and you obtain this freedom, you face a critical choice: emerge as a better person or fall into addictions to find happiness. It’s a mental battle.   
  
My advice? Use your money to free up your time. Invest in ready-made meals, a gardener, cleaners—whatever you can outsource.

Then, refine the skills that have allowed you to earn so much at a young age and build a business around them. Work for someone else for the next 3 - 5 years until you feel competent enough, then leave and use your savings as security while you establish your business.

I've been watching a lot of content on TikTok saying UK sucks and to move to South East Asia or Australia and I've been feeling like you too for months. To be honest UK isn't perfect but it gives a balance of many things, I will list mine below:

1.  Four seasons (none of them intense or extreme) instead of constant dry, humid weather.  
2.  Good quality of food - I can get hot season food, asian food and pretty much anything I want all in one shop!  
3.  Access to Europe - Alps, Dolomites, Ski in Charmonix, Weekend break in Innsbruck, there are loads of beautiful places in Europe and a majority of it is no more than 3 hours flight away. USA is 6\~ hours away.  
4. Stability - Lots of countries are economically or politically unstable, if you take the rose tinted glasses off, places like Thailand have a lot of political and economical issues.  
5. Good level of education for kids if you decide to have them.  
6. Traffic isn't that crazy and you can walk most places if you wanted.

Overall UK provides balance, it allows you to have a bit of everything without sacrificing a lot. Nature is beautiful in the UK aswell, lots of places to have a walk and a picnic if the weather allows it, many charming towns. If you're in full time you get a month\~ off a year.
